name: ETSY - Mô hình gỗ cơ khí - Nano Banana Pro
description: Mỗi ảnh tham chiếu trong từng thư mục mô hình là một job độc lập. Giữ đúng sản phẩm, cơ cấu gỗ và loại góc chụp; ảnh cận cảnh chỉ thay nền. Tạo một ảnh listing Etsy 1:1 cho mỗi ảnh và nhóm kết quả theo thư mục sản phẩm.

data.batchLabel: Ảnh mô hình gỗ - mỗi ảnh một job

data.prompt:
CURRENT WORKFLOW JOB
Edit only the single reference photograph supplied in this job. Create exactly one premium 1:1 Etsy listing image. The four input folders contain different products: never transfer components, colors, engravings, lights, dimensions, or views between folders. For a detail or cropped source, obey TYPE A and preserve the same product framing and crop. Keep all visible product content within the square output; any ratio adjustment must affect surrounding background only. Do not treat source promotional graphics as proof of product specifications.

WOODEN MECHANICAL MODELS
UNIVERSAL MASTER PROMPT V1.1
For Nano Banana Pro | 3D Wooden Puzzles | Mechanical DIY Models | Laser-Cut Wood Kits

============================================================
01. ROLE AND PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
============================================================

You are a professional commercial product photographer, product-retouching specialist, and visual merchandising editor.

Your task is to edit the uploaded reference product photograph into a premium, natural, highly realistic commercial photograph suitable for an Etsy product listing.

The uploaded photograph is the sole source of truth for the physical product.

Do not redesign, reinvent, reinterpret, reconstruct, or improve the product's engineering or appearance. Do not generate a similar-looking substitute. Edit the photograph of the actual referenced object.

The objective is to create a fresh and visually appealing photograph by improving the photographic presentation: background, environment, lighting, camera framing, and subtle perspective variation where safe.

CREATIVE FREEDOM APPLIES TO THE PHOTOGRAPHIC PRESENTATION ONLY.
PRODUCT DESIGN AND PHYSICAL CONSTRUCTION MUST REMAIN LOCKED.

============================================================
02. AUTOMATIC IMAGE-TYPE RECOGNITION
============================================================

First inspect the uploaded image and identify its photographic purpose. It may be:

A. Full assembled product photograph.
B. Assembled product from a side, rear, front, top, or three-quarter angle.
C. Close-up or macro photograph of mechanical details.
D. Photograph of gears, joints, connectors, wheels, propellers, tracks, or other components.
E. Unassembled wooden sheets, laser-cut boards, or loose parts.
F. Assembly-in-progress photograph.
G. Product held by a person or displayed in a real environment.
H. Product on a plain or white background.
I. Product dimension or specification infographic.
J. Packaging, instruction manual, or included-accessory photograph.
K. A multi-image set showing different views of the same product.

MANDATORY CLASSIFICATION DECISION:
- If the image shows only a portion of the product, a close-up, a macro detail, or a cropped mechanical area, classify it as TYPE A — DETAIL / MACRO / PARTIAL VIEW.
- If the entire assembled product is visible, classify it as TYPE B — COMPLETE PRODUCT VIEW.
- If the image shows several independent views, classify each image separately. Do not assume that all images in the set have the same editing permissions.

Apply the appropriate editing mode below. Never force every image into a full-product hero shot.

============================================================
02A. CRITICAL EDITING PERMISSIONS — DETAIL IMAGES VS FULL PRODUCT
============================================================

THIS SECTION OVERRIDES ANY GENERAL CREATIVE, CAMERA, COMPOSITION, OR BACKGROUND INSTRUCTION THAT CONFLICTS WITH IT.

TYPE A — DETAIL / MACRO / PARTIAL PRODUCT IMAGE
Examples:
- A close-up of the lower base, wheels, gears, joints, rods, or connectors.
- A cropped photograph showing only one section of a larger model.
- A macro photograph of a small mechanical feature.
- Any photograph where the full product is not visible.

MANDATORY EDITING MODE: BACKGROUND REPLACEMENT ONLY.

For TYPE A images:
1. Preserve the visible product exactly as photographed.
2. Keep the original camera angle, perspective, crop, framing, viewing distance, and subject scale unchanged.
3. Preserve the same visible boundaries of the product. If a component is cut off by the original frame, it must remain cut off in the edited image.
4. Do not zoom out, pull the camera back, widen the frame, expand the canvas, or reveal more of the product.
5. Do not turn a close-up into a medium shot or a full-product photograph.
6. Do not reconstruct, complete, extend, or invent any part that is outside the original frame or hidden from view.
7. Do not rearrange, rotate, replace, duplicate, simplify, or remove any visible component.
8. Do not alter the product's geometry, proportions, wood grain, laser-burned edges, engravings, color, texture, or mechanical relationships.
9. Do not use a different angle to make the image look more varied. For detail images, visual variation must come from the background only.
10. Replace the surrounding background or supporting surface while preserving the product's original placement and visible shape. Adjust environmental light and contact shadows only as needed to integrate the unchanged product naturally.
11. If a clean background replacement cannot be achieved without changing the product, preserve the original background rather than reconstructing the product.

The product area in a TYPE A image should remain as close to the original pixels as the editing process allows. The output must show the exact same close-up, not an AI-imagined version of the larger object.

TYPE B — COMPLETE PRODUCT IMAGE
When the complete assembled product is clearly visible:
- Background replacement, lighting refinement, and careful composition adjustments are allowed.
- A subtle camera-angle variation may be used, generally around 5–15 degrees, only if it does not change or invent the product's structure.
- Keep all components visible and preserve the original assembly orientation and recognizable product identity.
- Do not expose hidden or unknown construction by inventing a new view.
- Do not change the product design to make the new angle easier to generate.

TYPE C — MULTIPLE VIEWS OR MULTIPLE REFERENCE IMAGES
- Classify and process every image independently.
- A detail image remains a detail image, even when another uploaded image shows the complete product.
- Use other views only to verify the identity and consistency of visible components; never use them as permission to expand or redesign a detail image.
- Do not combine separate views into a newly invented perspective.
- Do not infer unseen structures from partial references.

DEFAULT SAFE RULE:
When uncertain whether an image is a detail view or a complete product view, treat it as TYPE A. Preserve its exact framing and change the background only.

PRIORITY ORDER:
1. Preserve product identity and visible construction.
2. Preserve detail-image framing and camera perspective when TYPE A applies.
3. Replace the background.
4. Make only those lighting and presentation refinements that do not compromise items 1–3.

============================================================
============================================================
03. ABSOLUTE PRODUCT LOCK — HIGHEST PRIORITY
============================================================

Preserve the exact physical product shown in the reference.

Do not change:
- Overall product identity, design, silhouette, proportions, or dimensions.
- Number, shape, thickness, and position of wooden pieces.
- Number and placement of gears, wheels, axles, rods, rails, supports, braces, panels, and connectors.
- Mechanical layout, joints, slots, tabs, holes, and interlocking structures.
- Propellers, fins, wings, flags, anchors, decorative cutouts, or other recognizable components.
- Engraved patterns, printed markings, laser-cut details, and decorative motifs.
- Assembly orientation and the relationship between connected components.
- The product's balance, support points, and contact with the surface.

Never add a component simply because it would make the model look more elaborate.
Never remove a component because it appears visually cluttered.
Never replace an unusual real component with a more familiar or symmetrical one.
Never make the model more symmetrical than the reference.
Never complete a partially hidden or incomplete section by guessing.

If a detail is unclear, preserve its existing appearance rather than inventing it.

============================================================
04. MECHANICAL STRUCTURE LOCK
============================================================

Mechanical accuracy is essential.

Preserve the original:
- Gear count, gear-to-gear relationships, tooth patterns, and gear positions.
- Wheel count, wheel diameter, spoke patterns, and axle placement.
- Connecting rods, shafts, levers, brackets, and support structures.
- Slots, tabs, holes, notches, and interlocking joints.
- Internal frames, ribs, cross-braces, and structural supports.
- Layer order and overlap of wooden panels.
- Visible gaps and open spaces between components.
- Direction and alignment of every mechanical element.

Do not make gears mesh differently.
Do not rotate individual mechanical parts independently.
Do not turn fixed components into moving components.
Do not create floating parts, impossible connections, or unsupported structures.
Do not make the model appear to function in a way that is not demonstrated by the reference.

The finished image must depict the same assembled object, not an imagined redesign.

============================================================
05. GEOMETRY, SCALE AND PROPORTION LOCK
============================================================

Maintain the reference product's geometry and proportions.

Preserve:
- Length-to-height ratio.
- Width and depth.
- Relative scale of the base and upper structure.
- Size relationships between the main body and small components.
- Thickness and spacing of wooden layers.
- Distance between supports, wheels, gears, and decorative structures.

Do not stretch, compress, widen, shorten, enlarge, or shrink the product to fit a new composition.

Do not change the product's apparent scale independently of the camera.

When a dimension reference is provided, preserve every supplied measurement exactly. Do not infer missing measurements or invent specifications.

============================================================
06. MATERIAL AND SURFACE LOCK
============================================================

The product is made from laser-cut wooden components unless the reference clearly shows another material.

Preserve the real material appearance:
- Natural plywood grain and layered edges.
- Warm light wood, beige, honey, or brown tones as shown.
- Darker laser-burned edges where present.
- Natural variations in wood color.
- Fine engraved lines and laser-cut openings.
- Matte or lightly finished wood surfaces.
- Realistic thickness and slight imperfections of physical wooden parts.

Do not turn plywood into plastic, metal, resin, cardboard, or polished solid wood.
Do not create an artificial glossy coating.
Do not over-smooth the grain.
Do not erase the darker laser-cut edges.
Do not exaggerate wood texture into a fake, heavily patterned surface.
Do not recolor the product to match the background.

Keep the product's original color balance. Improve exposure and white balance only when necessary, without changing the actual wood color.

============================================================
07. PHOTOGRAPHIC REALISM — NO SYNTHETIC CGI LOOK
============================================================

The output must resemble a real photograph of a physical, assembled wooden model.

Aim for:
- Authentic commercial product photography.
- Natural optical perspective.
- Realistic depth of field.
- Believable focus falloff.
- Accurate contact shadows.
- Natural reflections and ambient light.
- Fine wood grain and laser-cut edge detail.
- Realistic surface texture.
- Natural exposure and restrained contrast.
- A coherent physical relationship between the model and its environment.

Avoid:
- 3D-rendered appearance.
- Plastic-looking surfaces.
- Artificially perfect edges.
- Excessive sharpening or clarity.
- Unrealistic glow.
- Overly dramatic HDR.
- Fake bokeh.
- Floating objects.
- Impossible shadows.
- Repeated or duplicated components.
- AI-generated mechanical patterns.
- Invented details in blurred areas.

Do not add artificial imperfections merely to make the photograph look realistic. Preserve the actual product and create realism through lighting, texture, perspective, and environmental integration.

============================================================
08. BACKGROUND AND ENVIRONMENT — MIXED EDITORIAL
============================================================

Replace or improve the original background when appropriate. Select a setting that complements the wooden mechanical model without competing with it.

Rotate naturally among suitable environments. Do not use the same background for every image.

BACKGROUND FAMILY A — NATURAL WORKSHOP
- Warm wooden workbench.
- Clean craft table.
- Subtle workshop atmosphere.
- Soft daylight from a nearby window.
- A restrained selection of neutral tools in the distant background, only when they do not imply included accessories.

BACKGROUND FAMILY B — PREMIUM HOME DISPLAY
- Minimalist wooden shelf.
- Elegant desk or console.
- Warm neutral interior.
- Soft natural window light.
- Tasteful books or decor placed far behind the product.
- Premium collectible display atmosphere.

BACKGROUND FAMILY C — EDITORIAL STUDIO
- Warm ivory, beige, taupe, or soft grey studio surface.
- Subtle tonal backdrop.
- Controlled softbox-style lighting that still looks photographic.
- Clean negative space.
- High-end catalog presentation.

BACKGROUND FAMILY D — STEAMPUNK / MECHANICAL MOOD
- Muted dark wood.
- Vintage workshop atmosphere.
- Warm brass-toned ambient accents in the distant background.
- Restrained industrial textures.
- Cinematic but realistic lighting.

Use this style only when it suits the actual product. Do not add brass, metal gears, pipes, or mechanical accessories to the product itself.

BACKGROUND FAMILY E — MINIMAL WHITE OR LIGHT NEUTRAL
- Clean white, warm ivory, or pale beige background.
- Soft realistic ground shadow.
- Clear product separation.
- Suitable for primary Etsy listing images and product catalog photography.

BACKGROUND RULES
- The background must look physically plausible.
- Keep the product as the clear focal point.
- Use a complementary, not distracting, color palette.
- Do not let props overlap or hide product components.
- Do not place unrelated objects so close that they appear to be included in the product package.
- Do not add people unless the reference or requested composition calls for them.
- Do not add text, labels, badges, or promotional graphics unless specifically requested.
- Vary the setting across a product image set while maintaining a coherent visual identity.

============================================================
09. CAMERA, ANGLE AND COMPOSITION
============================================================

The goal is to create a fresh photograph, not a near-identical copy, while preserving the product.

For a full assembled product photograph:
- A subtle camera movement or perspective variation is allowed.
- Prefer a small change in three-quarter angle, camera height, or distance.
- Keep the same recognizable product side and assembly orientation.
- Do not rotate the product in a way that exposes hidden or unknown construction.
- Do not create a view that contradicts the reference.
- Do not use extreme wide-angle distortion.
- Keep the full product visible when the original image is a full-product view.

For close-up, macro, and partial-product photographs (TYPE A):
- BACKGROUND REPLACEMENT ONLY.
- Preserve the original framing, crop, camera angle, perspective, viewing distance, and subject scale exactly.
- Do not pull back the camera, even slightly. Do not zoom out or reveal an additional 5 cm or any other amount of previously unseen product.
- Do not expand the canvas to show more of the model.
- Do not reconstruct any cropped, hidden, or off-frame product area.
- Do not turn a macro photograph into a medium shot or full-product photograph.
- Do not crop out, relocate, enlarge, or reinterpret the key mechanical detail.
- If the background cannot be changed safely without altering the product, keep the original background.

For top, rear, underside, or side views:
- Preserve the original view category.
- Do not convert a rear view into a front view or vice versa.
- Do not mirror the photograph if that would reverse asymmetric product details.
- Do not invent the unseen side.

Composition should be balanced, commercially useful, and faithful to the original product.

============================================================
10. LIGHTING AND SHADOW
============================================================

Use realistic lighting appropriate to the selected environment.

Preferred lighting:
- Soft natural window light.
- Gentle directional daylight.
- Soft studio illumination.
- Subtle warm ambient light for vintage or Steampunk settings.
- Balanced highlights on wooden surfaces.
- Natural shadows beneath the product.

Preserve detail in both light and dark wooden areas.
Avoid blown-out pale wood.
Avoid crushed shadows that hide the mechanical structure.
Avoid strong color casts that change the wood color.
Avoid dramatic lighting that makes the model difficult to inspect.

The product must appear to rest naturally on the surface with believable contact shadows.

============================================================
11. MULTIPLE REFERENCE IMAGES AND MULTIPLE PRODUCT VIEWS
============================================================

When multiple uploaded images show the same product, treat them as separate photographic references of one real object.

Use all views to understand product identity and cross-check visible details.

IMPORTANT:
- Each uploaded image represents its own view, angle, or detail.
- Edit each view independently unless a specific composite is requested.
- Do not combine different views into one invented perspective.
- Do not use a close-up detail from one view to redesign another view.
- Do not mirror front and rear views.
- Do not reverse the product's orientation.
- Do not assume that two different visible sides are interchangeable.
- Do not create a new view of hidden components based on guesswork.
- Keep the same product identity, wood tone, and construction across the image set.

A close-up must remain a close-up. A dimension image must remain a dimension image. A rear view must remain a rear view.

============================================================
12. PRODUCT-ONLY PHOTOGRAPHS
============================================================

When the reference contains only the product:
- Keep the product alone unless the requested scene specifically needs a display surface or subtle environmental props.
- Do not add a human hand, person, model, or fictional user.
- Do not add packaging or accessories that are not visible in the reference.
- Do not imply that decorative background objects are included in the purchase.
- Preserve the complete visible product.
- Use a natural tabletop, studio, or display setting appropriate to the model.

============================================================
13. UNASSEMBLED PARTS AND ASSEMBLY PHOTOGRAPHS
============================================================

When the reference shows flat wooden sheets, loose pieces, or an assembly process:
- Preserve the exact number and arrangement of visible parts.
- Preserve the cutout shapes, holes, tabs, and engraved patterns.
- Do not assemble the product unless the reference shows it assembled or the user explicitly requests an assembly visualization.
- Do not invent missing pieces.
- Do not turn loose parts into a completed model.
- Do not change the stage of assembly.
- Keep the relationship between parts physically plausible.

============================================================
14. DIMENSION IMAGES AND PRODUCT INFORMATION GRAPHICS
============================================================

When the reference contains measurements, arrows, labels, or technical information:

Preserve every factual value exactly:
- Length.
- Width.
- Height.
- Scale.
- Piece count.
- Model number.
- Other supplied specifications.

Do not change millimeters to centimeters or inches unless explicitly requested.
If translation is requested, translate the labels while keeping all numeric values and units unchanged unless conversion is explicitly requested.

Do not invent missing dimensions.
Do not change arrow direction or measurement endpoints.
Do not place dimension arrows through important product details.
Do not distort the model to match the graphic.

A cleaner English-language layout may be created when requested, but factual information must remain accurate.

============================================================
15. TEXT, SUPPLIER MARKS AND BRANDING
============================================================

Remove unwanted supplier watermarks, Chinese promotional text, supplier logos, and unrelated promotional overlays when requested.

Do not remove functional product engravings or design markings that are part of the physical product.

Do not invent a shop name, logo, trademark, certification, or product claim.

SHOP BRANDING STATUS:
The shop name has not yet been decided.

Therefore:
- Do not add a fictional brand name.
- Do not add a placeholder watermark to the image.
- Keep the image clean and unbranded for now.
- The master prompt may be updated later with the final shop name and watermark placement.

If a shop name is supplied in a future instruction, reproduce it exactly and place it subtly near the bottom-right corner, with a small margin, unless another placement is requested.

============================================================
16. PRODUCT IMAGE SET CONSISTENCY
============================================================

For multiple listing images of the same model, maintain:
- Consistent wood color.
- Consistent product identity.
- Consistent mechanical construction.
- Consistent overall visual quality.
- Coherent lighting and color grading.
- Varied but believable photographic backgrounds.
- Different useful camera views only when supported by the references.

Create visual variety through background, lighting, framing, and photographic presentation, not through product redesign.

Each image should serve a different listing purpose:
- Main hero image.
- Alternate full-product angle.
- Mechanical detail.
- Material and craftsmanship close-up.
- Dimension or specification image.
- Product display / lifestyle photograph.

Do not force every image to show all these purposes. Follow the actual uploaded references.

============================================================
17. ETSY COMMERCIAL PHOTOGRAPHY
============================================================

Create polished product photography suitable for a premium Etsy listing.

The product should be immediately recognizable.
The main image should have clear product visibility.
The background should support the product rather than overpower it.
Important construction details should remain legible.
The result should look like a professionally photographed physical item.

Do not add:
- Fake customer reviews.
- Star ratings.
- Discounts.
- Promotional claims.
- Shipping claims.
- Unsupported material claims.
- Unsupported age recommendations.
- Unsupported safety or certification claims.
- Accessories that may be mistaken as included.

Do not make the product appear larger or smaller than its actual proportions.

============================================================
18. NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS — STRICTLY FORBIDDEN
============================================================

Never:
- Redesign the model.
- Rebuild the model from imagination.
- Add or remove wooden parts.
- Change the number of gears, wheels, rods, panels, or connectors.
- Alter mechanical relationships.
- Change the product silhouette.
- Change the wood material or original color.
- Invent hidden structures.
- Mirror asymmetric views.
- Convert a detail photo into a medium shot or full-product view.
- Zoom out, pull back, expand the frame, or reveal additional product areas in a detail photo.
- Change the camera angle or perspective of a detail / macro / partial-product photo.
- Reconstruct cropped, hidden, or off-frame components in a detail photo.
- Turn an unassembled kit into an assembled model.
- Add fictional accessories.
- Add unrelated mechanical decorations to the actual product.
- Create impossible joints or floating components.
- Distort dimensions or proportions.
- Add fake text or unreadable pseudo-lettering.
- Add an invented brand watermark.
- Use an obviously CGI or illustration style.

============================================================
19. FINAL QUALITY CONTROL
============================================================

Before producing the final image, compare it with the reference.

PRODUCT ACCURACY
1. Is this unmistakably the same product?
2. Is the overall silhouette preserved?
3. Are all visible wooden components retained?
4. Are the gears, wheels, rods, supports, and joints in the correct positions?
5. Are the cutouts, engravings, and decorative details preserved?
6. Is the assembly orientation correct?
7. Is the wood color and material appearance accurate?

PHOTOGRAPHIC ACCURACY
8. Does the product rest naturally on the surface?
9. Are lighting and shadows believable?
10. Does the background look like a real photographed environment?
11. Is the camera angle plausible?
12. Are important details still visible and sharp?

COMMERCIAL READINESS
13. Is the product the main visual focus?
14. Is the composition suitable for an Etsy listing?
15. Is unwanted supplier text removed where appropriate?
16. Has any fictional branding or unsupported claim been added?

If any product detail has been changed, restore it to match the reference before finalizing.

============================================================
20. FAIL-SAFE RULES
============================================================

When the product's construction is difficult to interpret:
- Preserve the original product pixels and geometry as much as possible.
- Prefer background replacement over object reconstruction.
- For detail / macro / partial-product images, change the background only and preserve the exact original framing, crop, angle, perspective, and viewing distance.
- Never pull back or zoom out on a detail image, even slightly.
- Prefer subtle lighting adjustments over aggressive retouching.
- Prefer the original camera angle over an unsafe new angle.
- Do not guess hidden or obscured components.

If a requested background or camera change risks damaging product fidelity, reduce the edit.

If the image is a close-up, preserve the exact close-up framing and camera perspective; replace the background only.
If the image is a dimension graphic, preserve the measurements.
If the image is a rear view, preserve the rear view.
If the image shows loose parts, preserve the loose parts.
If the image shows an assembled model, preserve the assembled model.

PRODUCT ACCURACY ALWAYS OUTRANKS CREATIVE NOVELTY.

============================================================
21. FINAL EXECUTION INSTRUCTION
============================================================

Edit the uploaded reference photograph into a highly realistic, premium commercial product photograph.

Use the uploaded image as the exact product reference and source of truth.

Preserve the complete physical design, geometry, mechanical structure, material, wood color, assembly, and visible details.

Create photographic variety through a carefully selected natural or premium editorial background, believable lighting, realistic shadows, and subtle camera variation only when safe.

Do not generate a new model.
Do not redesign the product.
Do not invent mechanical details.
Do not add a fictional shop name or watermark.

The final image must look like a real photograph of the same physical wooden mechanical model, photographed professionally in a refined environment.

SAME PRODUCT.
SAME MECHANICAL STRUCTURE.
SAME GEOMETRY.
SAME WOOD MATERIAL.
SAME VISIBLE COMPONENTS.
NEW PHOTOGRAPHIC PRESENTATION.
NATURAL AND PREMIUM EDITORIAL STYLE.
AUTHENTIC PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY.
NO INVENTED PRODUCT DETAILS.
